MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Service

Patient: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]
Referring Clinician: Dr. [redacted name]
Date of Report: [redacted date]

REFERRAL REASON
Predictive testing for CADASIL (Cerebral Autosomal Dominant Arteriopathy with Subcortical Infarcts and Leukoencephalopathy). Patient's father diagnosed with CADASIL and carries the pathogenic NOTCH3 c.421C>T p.(Arg141Cys) variant.

METHODOLOGY
Targeted Sanger sequencing was performed to detect the familial NOTCH3 variant c.421C>T p.(Arg141Cys). Genomic DNA was extracted from peripheral blood. PCR amplification of NOTCH3 exon 4 was performed followed by bidirectional fluorescent Sanger sequencing. Analysis was performed using reference sequence NM_000435.3.

RESULTS
NOTCH3 (NM_000435.3): c.421C>T p.(Arg141Cys) - NOT DETECTED

The familial pathogenic variant was not identified in this patient's sample. Sequencing coverage was adequate across the target region with high quality scores.

SUMMARY
This adult male patient has tested negative for the familial NOTCH3 c.421C>T p.(Arg141Cys) variant associated with CADASIL in his father. The absence of this variant indicates the patient has not inherited the familial mutation and is therefore highly unlikely to develop CADASIL. The risk to this patient is considered to be equivalent to the general population risk.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. No specific surveillance for CADASIL is indicated for this patient
2. Other at-risk family members remain eligible for predictive testing
3. Genetic counseling is recommended for all family members considering predictive testing
4. This result should be communicated to the patient in the context of post-test genetic counseling

This test was performed in an accredited laboratory (CPA accreditation number: [redacted ID])

Authorized by: Dr. [redacted name], Consultant Clinical Scientist
Date: [redacted date]
